pointsOfInterest.name: Freeman Store & Museum
pointsOfInterest.description: Built in 1859 as the Lydecker Store, this building later served as a Civil War hospital and as offices for both Union and Confederate armies. It is now Vienna's volunteer-run store and museum.

pointsOfInterest.name: Vienna Train Depot & Caboose
pointsOfInterest.description: The Vienna Depot served the town for 109 years on the Alexandria, Loudoun & Hampshire Railroad and its successor, the W&OD Railway, until rail service ended in 1968.

pointsOfInterest.name: Historic Little Library
pointsOfInterest.description: This small former library building is maintained by Historic Vienna, Inc. It connects today's readers to the town's civic and cultural history.

pointsOfInterest.name: First Baptist Church of Vienna
pointsOfInterest.description: The former First Baptist Church is among Vienna's recognized historic places. Its story is part of the town's enduring Black community and post-Civil War heritage.
